definition: An IPv4 VPC block can range from slash 16, about 65,000 addresses, down to slash 28, 16 addresses. Remember: plan non-overlapping ranges if you will peer or connect on-premises.
AWS reserves 5 addresses in every subnet: the first four and the last one. Remember: a slash 27 subnet gives only 27 usable addresses, not 32.
NAT gateway: managed, scales to 100 Gbps, redundant within one zone, no security groups. NAT instance: self-managed EC2, disable source destination check, supports security groups.

A single NAT gateway that automatically expands across Availability Zones where you have workloads. Needs no public subnet and one route table target. Remember: public connectivity only, not private NAT.
Security groups: instance level, stateful, allow rules only, all rules evaluated. Network ACLs: subnet level, stateless, allow and deny rules, evaluated in number order, first match wins.
Clients receive responses on temporary high ports, typically 1024 to 65535. Remember: because network ACLs are stateless, you must allow these ports for return traffic.
Private connection between two VPCs, even across accounts or Regions. No overlapping CIDRs, and update both route tables. Remember: not transitive, so each pair needs its own peering.
Gateway endpoint: route table target, S3 and DynamoDB only, free, not reachable from on-premises. Interface endpoint: ENI with private IP, most services, paid, reachable over VPN and Direct Connect.
Exposes one VPC's service to many consumer VPCs through interface endpoints, fronted by a Network Load Balancer. Remember: no peering, overlapping CIDRs are fine, consumers reach only that service.
Regional hub that connects thousands of VPCs, VPNs and Direct Connect with transitive routing. Share across accounts with AWS RAM. Remember: choose it for IP multicast and ECMP VPN bandwidth.

Encrypted IPsec tunnels over the internet. AWS side: virtual private gateway or transit gateway. Your side: customer gateway device. Remember: enable route propagation; CloudHub links multiple branch sites.
Private dedicated network link to AWS, often weeks to provision. Not encrypted by default: add an IPsec VPN over it, or MACsec on 10 Gbps and faster dedicated ports.
Global resource that lets one Direct Connect connection reach VPCs in many Regions and accounts. Remember: it does not route traffic between the VPCs attached to it.
High resiliency: one connection at each of two locations. Maximum resiliency: two connections on separate devices at each of two locations. Cheapest backup: a Site-to-Site VPN.
Logs IP traffic metadata, not packets, for a VPC, subnet or network interface. Sends to CloudWatch Logs, S3 or Data Firehose. Remember: inbound accepted, outbound rejected means a network ACL.
IPv6-only gateway that allows outbound connections and blocks connections started from the internet. Remember: it is the IPv6 counterpart of a NAT gateway.
Managed firewall for whole VPCs at layers 3 to 7: stateful rules, domain filtering, intrusion prevention. Remember: WAF protects web apps; Network Firewall protects the VPC.
Inbound data is free. Same-zone traffic over private IPs is free; cross-zone and public IP traffic is charged. Remember: use an S3 gateway endpoint instead of NAT.
